ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT REPORT
Date of Inspection: February 1, 2026
Property: 456 Oak Ave, Oklahoma City OK

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
This property was inspected following a storm event on January 10, 2026 with recorded wind gusts of 65 mph. We observed several areas of lifted shingles, creased tabs, and unsealed tabs along the windward elevation. However, our analysis concludes the damage is attributable to deterioration and loss of seal due to normal aging rather than the reported wind event.

FINDINGS:
Multiple shingles exhibited adhesive failure along the seal strip. We observed crease marks on several tab edges. The thermal sealing on the south-facing slope appeared compromised. The roof system is approximately 12 years old, and the seal strip adhesion has degraded with age. Hand seal testing was not performed. We did not correlate damage patterns with recorded prevailing wind direction. No wind speed analysis was conducted for the specific microclimate of this property.

The shingle manufacturer rates these shingles for wind resistance per ASTM D3161 Class F (110 mph). Since the recorded wind speeds were below this threshold, the shingles should have resisted the wind forces experienced.

CONCLUSION:
The tab lifting and creasing are the result of normal aging, wear and tear, and deferred maintenance of the seal strip. The storm event did not cause the observed conditions. We recommend the homeowner re-seal or replace individual tabs as part of routine maintenance.
